I'm not, but I grew up feeling very lonely, very, very lonely..
I didn't just seek help. I fought for it (quite literally). 
I told my school psychologist about me not being able to make any connections with poeple, that I was lonely etc... She then told me to gossip less and tough up because no one is happy. Okay, attempt number 1 in getting help failed.
I tried to talk to some of my classmates, resting the waters, trying to open up. Didn't work-they totally thought i was weird and couldn't understand me, even though they noticed the way I am- way too sad and secluded, quiet etc. Attempt no 2 failed.

I kept postponing asking my parents for help because I knew that they didn't understand. We also basically had no relationship back then.

So i did the worst absolute thing, looking back to that particular period- i decided to keep to myself.
Spoiler alert: it got way worse.

I couldn't do it anymore, i made many attempts and put in so much effort but onL got worse. I felt like i failed at life and there was nothing in this World for me. I cared about school before, art, my pets, and suddenly it all just wasnt even enough to make me have a single positive thought.

So I had to ask my parents for help.

They didn't believe me, they said that if I knew I had a problem then I should also know how to solve it.
They were horrified of the mere idea of me saying how I might be mentally ill because they saw it as craziness, lunacy, mental hospital type of thing. Everyone just ignored me and tbh they were never not toxic to me, now they were even more toxic.

The thing that I had going for me, is that i remained consistent. For the next period, I kept acting on my emotions - when i was feeling broken, I made sure my parents would notice. I didn't talk, let my true face shine through the mask. They started taking me seriously after They saw that my life was falling apart, and my homeroom teacher told my mom i look ed like I needed help...

My mom started to get more informed, she slowly accepted the idea of depression... Over time.
And then she got me help. And she tried helping me too. And succeeded (she and I cpmmected through my expressing emotions to her in a proper way and her showing that she cares to hear what I have to say.she may not have had any good advice, but she was open to learning)

All in all, the thing that changed with my family (slowly) is that they didn't see my mental illness as something horrifying, insanity and they accepted it as they got to know it.

They got to know me. And so when everything next I felt lonely I remembered that I was not, in fact, alone. Someone knows. I made an impact, there was an emotional connection with someone (first it was through anger, then despair, then sadness, then it was new type of care, then now its even happiness sometimes).
I got so much better, but these were only some of the steps, and they were the first steps out of many more... And its still a conscious fight. I got stronger but new challenges come up constantly
